text:
Predicates:
Deadly(x) ::: x is a deadly disease.
LowSurvivalRate(x) ::: x comes with a low survival rate.
SevereCancer(x) ::: x is a severe cancer.
BileDuctCancer(x) ::: x is a bile duct cancer.
Cancer(x) ::: x is a cancer.
MildFlu(x) ::: x is a mild flu.
ColorectalCancer(x) ::: x is a colorectal cancer.
Premises:
∀x (Deadly(x) → LowSurvivalRate(x)) ::: If something is a deadly disease, then it comes with a low survival rate.
∀x (SevereCancer(x) → Deadly(x)) ::: Severe cancers are deadly diseases.
∀x (BileDuctCancer(x) → Cancer(x)) ::: Bile duct cancer is a severe form of cancer.
∀x (Cholangiocarcinoma(x) → BileDuctCancer(x)) ::: All Cholangiocarcinoma is bile duct cancer.
∀x (MildFlu(x) → LowSurvivalRate(x)) ::: Mild flu comes with a low survival rate.
¬(BileDuctCancer(colorectalCancer) ∧ LowSurvivalRate(colorectalCancer)) ::: Colorectal cancer is not both a bile duct cancer and with a low survival rate.
Conclusion:
SevereCancer(colorectalCancer) ::: Colorectal cancer is a kind of severe cancer.
